name: Noisy Dish
_comment_group: A show under the Snapchat heading, cut to Conspiracy Central's
design, with its own faces and colours. Shared with that pack: the
frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated 40px, the twenty
characters to a line, the freeform text box, the drag, the card, and
a dark shade from the foot of the frame that the Gradient button
switches per frame.
The faces and the colours are this show's own. The block is set in
Bebas Neue Cyrillic like its model's, but a picked word comes out in
Montserrat Regular rather than Poppins; and the palette is black,
white, a cyan, a deep red, a pink and a yellow, which the user pairs
between the type and the card. Each is argued where it is stated.
One thing of Conspiracy Central's the show did NOT ask for, and it
is left out on purpose rather than forgotten: the shade arrives
OFF. It is there for the frame that needs it, a press away, rather
than laid over every still by default; argued at `branding` below.
The caption stands where every Snapchat caption stands, on the foot
of the frame at the preset's margin (see `layout` below).
It used to be a different design altogether: the still shrunk to 85%
and laid as a rounded card on a crimson-to-amber ground, tinted brick
along its foot, with white Bebas Neue under it held off the amber by
an opaque shadow and no palette at all. The show asked to look like
Conspiracy Central instead, so the `photo` key, its backdrop and its
tint are gone and the pack was rewritten from that one rather than
edited from its own past. git history has the old numbers and the
argument for each of them, if the show ever asks for the ground back.
Written as its own folder rather than as an override of a sibling,
for the reason content/README.md gives: a channel is a folder that
gets dropped in, and a pack that leans on another one's file for its
look breaks the day that other show changes its mind - which is
exactly what Conspiracy Central has already done once.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Bebas Neue Cyrillic, with picked words in Montserrat Regular, in six
colours the user pairs per frame, on a card. The card, its shape,
the size, where the lines break and the capitals are the Snapchat
caption design and are stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json.
What changing the design meant for this pack in particular is that
the card came back, and what follows from a card is written once, in
content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its caption on the
photograph may take the card back'. Here it meant one thing more:
the shadow this pack stated was OPAQUE black, chosen against a known
amber ground that no longer exists, and it goes with the ground -
removing the key lets the preset's `null` through, which is right
for type on a solid card somebody chose.
Like Conspiracy Central, and unlike the nine packs that README
section is about, this show REPLACED its look rather than adding
colours to it: its old white is in the list only because the show
asked for an absolute white, not as a swatch kept to undo a choice.
The list is the six colours in the order they were asked for.
Uppercased, inherited from the preset, and this pack could not
sensibly turn it off: Bebas has no lower case of its own, so a
caption in Montserrat's lower case would have its block in capitals
and its picked words not, and the highlight would be carrying a
difference nobody chose.

_comment_face: Bebas Neue Cyrillic - the face Conspiracy Central is set in, and
a different file from the Bebas Neue this pack used to state,
with a family name of its own. content/faces/bebas-neue-cyrillic.json
says why that name is what keeps the two from being drawn as one
A tall condensed display face whose capitals fill the em. On a
card it needs nothing else to hold it, which is the job the
opaque shadow was doing when the type stood on the amber ground.
_comment_color: White, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no colour
of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor).
True #FFFFFF - the absolute white the show asked for, and the
same white this pack has always been set in. It is also the
colour of a picked word - see `highlight` - so the whole caption
is one colour until the highlight row is pressed, and what
separates a picked word is the face.
_comment_colors: Absolute black, absolute white, the cyan #5DF9ED, the deep red
#A70B0B, the pink #FF75D1 and the yellow #FAFF00, in the order the
show gave them, offered for the letters and for the card behind
them - six buttons each in the title panel (see
editor.renderColorButtons). Written in capitals because every hex
in these packs is; the colours are exactly the ones asked for.
The same six in both lists and in one order, which is what Hall
of Femme and Conspiracy Central do and for their reason: the point
is the PAIRING. White on black is what the channel opens on; black
on cyan, on pink and on yellow, and white on the red, are a button
away. Six is as many as justice-oclock offers, and the panel lays
them out without anything else changing.
Nothing stops the user setting black on black, or black on the
red, which is too dark to carry it. The two lists are independent
because the pairing is the feature, and the user can see the
caption has gone and presses another swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block, as a row of
its own - see the note on `colors` in js/channels.js. Until that
row is pressed on a frame, picked words follow the block.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Montserrat Regular, in the same white as
the rest of the block. The colour is stated and it is the block's,
so the recolour draws exactly what its neighbours are drawn in and
the FACE is the whole of the difference until the user gives the
picked words a colour of their own from the highlight row.
The move Conspiracy Central makes with Poppins, made with
Montserrat: Bebas is the block, and a picked word comes out wide,
round and lighter than the words either side of it, which changes
the shape of the line and not only its texture. Montserrat's
capitals are a touch wider and more geometric than Poppins', so
the picked word is if anything further from the block. That the
two faces set at one size come out at two apparent sizes costs
nothing here: the preset states `fontSize`, so there is no
per-line fit for the wider face to win (see the note on two faces
in content/README.md).
It also undoes the oldest decision in this pack. It used to have
no highlight at all, because Bebas Neue shipped as one cut and the
type was white on every frame; a second face is the answer it had
no room for then.
Colour mode, word scope and no shadow are the preset's and are
not restated.
_comment_panel: Black, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
Black because it is the first colour the show asked for and the
white type reads on it at once. The pack used to state `panel:
null` - the still was a card of its own and a slab on top of it
would have been a background in front of a background - and that
argument went with the photo card.
_comment_layout: No `layout` of its own: the preset's block, stood on the foot of
the frame at its 120px margin, where every Snapchat caption
stands - Conspiracy Central's included, since that pack came down
from the head of the frame. The key is left out and the preset's
answer comes through whole, with the reasoning it gives for that
margin (the player's furniture along the bottom edge).
Stated by absence rather than by restating the preset's numbers,
for the reason the capture note gives: a pack that copies a shared
answer is a pack that can be left behind when the answer moves.

_comment_scrim: Conspiracy Central's shade, number for number: black at 0.65 at the
foot of the frame, falling in a straight line to nothing at half its
height, over the photograph and under the card. That pack explains
why those two stops are the Thumbnail Maker's dark gradient turned
on its side, and what of the backend's ramp a fixed scrim cannot
copy; nothing about the numbers is different here.
The caption stands on the foot of the frame, as that pack's does,
so the shade rises from under the card and is a shadow behind the
caption as much as a darkening of the picture.
It ends on a fully transparent stop, so there is no line across the
_comment_branding: `gradient` is false: the shade is OFFERED, not laid on. Every frame
arrives clean, and the Gradient button under the canvas switches
the scrim above on for the frame that wants it - instantly, on the
canvas, with no round trip (see editor.toggleGradient). The button
is there because the channel has a scrim, not because of this flag
(see editor.syncGradientButton), so off by default does not mean
Off where Conspiracy Central has it on, and that is the show's
call: the caption already sits on a solid card, so the shade is not
what keeps it legible, and the show wanted it as a choice per frame
rather than a look on every one.
On this channel the flag means the SCRIM rather than the backend's
side gradient, as on conspiracy-central and laugh-society-snapchat;
the backend is never asked for its ramp as well (see
state.backendPresentation), so a still is never darkened twice.
